rubric.result: The objective's three promises are each produced by lines of the diff. Read: EpicGroomClient.read() fetches '/epic-groom' and projects the body into the seven kinds (none, no-spec, draft, awaiting-publication, groomable, groomed, authorised), with useEpicGroom driving it from mount. Run the groom: EpicGroomClient.groom(key) POSTs '/epic-groom'. Press the promotion: EpicGroomClient.promote(key) POSTs '/epic-promotion'. Both presses carry the handed key in the x-gate-key header and no body, and the key itself only ever comes from the read (key: string | null on groomable and groomed). Nothing the objective names is missing.

The **TDD:** line names it('stops asking once there is something to press and keeps asking while it waits') in useEpicGroom.test.ts, and the sentence that fixes the limit is 'with awaiting-publication the timer fires again, and once the answer is groomable no further request is made'. The test in the diff is that test: fetch is doubled with two awaiting-publication answers and then groomable; after each advanceTimersByTimeAsync(POLL_INTERVAL_MS) the count is asserted 2, then 3, then 3 again. The assertion is on the fetch double (expect(reading).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3)) and not on the hook's returned value, so deleting 'if (restsAt(outcome)) return' from useEpicGroom.ts makes a fourth request happen and the last assertion turns red: the test can fail for the reason its name gives. Its boundary pair, it('a groomable body with no key reads as a state with no key rather than as unavailable'), is in client.test.ts and asserts the full groomable outcome with key: null.

The Contract block for frontend/src/app/epic-groom/EpicGroom.types.ts is reproduced name by name: GroomPlanIssue (order, title, labels), EpicIssue (number, url, title, status), the nine members of EpicGroomOutcome with 'key: string | null' on groomable and groomed, no key on authorised, and refused carrying {code, error}; EpicGroomAskOutcome with acted (status 'groomed' | 'authorised', milestone, issues, promoted: number[]), refused and backend-unreachable. The task's prose contract holds too: both presses send POST with headers { 'x-gate-key': key } and no body (asserted literally in client.test.ts), a 200 whose status is groomed or authorised is acted, anything else that is not {code, detail} is backend-unreachable, a fetch that throws is unavailable on the read and backend-unreachable on either press, and POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10000 is declared once in useEpicGroom.ts.

D-22 is the row this diff bears on, and it implements the value stated: the gates are pressed from the page with the key it was handed, so groom() and promote() both send x-gate-key, and the key the page can send is only the one the read minted for it. D-6 holds: the presses are acts of the app through its own endpoints. D-7 holds by absence: no merge call, no write to a pull request, no merge button in this module. D-13 holds: the hook stores no phase, it derives one read at a time from the endpoint and rests, it never journals a state. The remaining rows (D-1, D-10, D-11, D-18, D-21, D-23, D-14, D-25) have no subject in a frontend client and the diff leaves them alone.

Exemplars. I opened frontend/src/app/spec-freeze/client.ts, useSpecFreeze.ts, SpecFreezeMother.ts, client.test.ts and useSpecFreeze.test.ts, and app/implement-progress/useImplementProgress.ts. The diff plays the same roles with the same idiom: type guards over an unknown body, toOutcome/asRefusal, PATH and header constants, the exported object of functions, the hook's cancelled/timer effect with window.setTimeout(poll, 0) and a cleanup that clears it. Fixtures: I verified them against backend/API.md rather than taking the claim. The groomable body matches API.md's GET /epic-groom example exactly (milestone 'The loop enters through brainstorming', plan.issues order 1 'The intermediate gate retires' with type:backend/area:api/status:backlog and order 2 'The session channel' with type:ui/area:sessions/status:backlog); the promoted body matches POST /epic-promotion's 200 including "promoted":[348,349]; groomedByThePress matches EpicGroomRoute.grooming's Answer.send (status, milestone, issues, no key, no promoted); notFromThePage's 403 and detail are literally EpicGroomRoute.#NOT_FROM_THE_PAGE_DETAIL. The only value not documented literally is the 64-hex KEY, which API.md prints truncated as '3f9c1a...'. Rules to obey. frontend/README.md and frontend-engineering:frontend-best-practices (loaded) are satisfied: client.ts in the feature folder, EpicGroom.types.ts, useEpicGroom.ts, EpicGroomMother.ts under src/__scenarios__, PascalCase exported object, no semicolons, named exports, absolute imports, no comments, null for intentional absence, vitest globals not imported. conventions/defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary - the answers are discriminated unions on 'kind', the wire status is read at the door into that vocabulary and never compared by hand afterwards, and the two loose strings that remain (EpicIssue.status, refused.code) are the Contract block's own wording and are carried, never dispatched on; (2) raw map as the return value of logic - no subject: every function returns a declared union, and the mother's {status, body} pairs are test scaffolding of a wire payload; (3) two fields that have to agree / sentinel - key is 'string | null' with the absence in the type, not an empty string, and promoted: [] is the empty set rather than a sentinel (API.md itself documents [] for 'nothing was waiting', and a groom press promotes nothing by definition); (4) an error named for where it happens - no subject: the failure members are unavailable, backend-unreachable and refused, each named for what happened. boundaries.md: the body is validated by projection of exactly the keys consumed, with type predicates and no cast. architecture.md/domain.md/decisions.md: one concept per module, the types beside their client, no rule of the backend's restated here. simplicity.md: every exported symbol has a caller - the twelve mother scenarios and ten constants are all consumed by the two test files, and the client's consumer is task 12's panel in this same slice. THE DECLARED JUDGEMENT CALL, ruled: useEpicGroom is a module-level hook with a readonly RESTING_KINDS array and a restsAt predicate, and conventions/style.md says 'No free function at module level: every function hangs off a type'. I rule it not a finding, for three reasons that are written down rather than mine: the repository's own CLAUDE.md, which the plan names under Rules to obey, says of ct's two remaining style rules 'no prose in the code, and no free function at module level - keep their exemption here. They are a different piece of work', in the same section where it refuses the exemption for language; section 3 names useSpecFreeze.ts and useImplementProgress.ts as files to imitate and useImplementProgress.ts already carries the identical shape (DELIVERY_STEPS readonly array plus isAwaitingReviewer/isFinal predicates); and frontend/src holds zero production classes, so a lone class-wrapped hook is exactly the 'half a migration reads worse than none' the document argues against. The client's exported surface does hang off EpicGroomClient, the namespace architecture.md tolerates. Two tensions I found and leave out of the findings because the plan's own text ordered the shape ('the same shape as app/spec-freeze/client.ts'): the module-level test helpers answerWith/responseFor, which testing.md lists as an antipattern but which are the named exemplar's own shape; and press() reading response.json() outside its try while read() reads it inside, so a press answered with a body that is not JSON rejects instead of becoming backend-unreachable - the exemplar spec-freeze/client.ts has the same asymmetry and the plan's sentence only covers 'a fetch that throws'.

No subject. The staged diff is six files, all 'new file mode 100644', 429 insertions and 0 deletions: there is not a single '-' line, so no pre-existing assertion, case or test could have been removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. client.ts holds the whole parse (the seven kinds, keyOf, the refusal reading, the press's acted/refused/backend-unreachable split) and useEpicGroom.ts holds the timer, the POLL_INTERVAL_MS and the decision to stop at the three actionable rungs. The only double in either test file is the global fetch, which is the boundary the page really crosses; EpicGroomMother supplies wire bodies and no behaviour. Every one of the eight tests dies if the production module it exercises is reverted - in particular the stop-polling test asserts the request production code did not make, not a value the test wrote. The client has no production consumer yet, which is the plan's slicing and not scaffolding: task 12 of this plan is the panel that reads useEpicGroom.

The six paths written are exactly the six the **Files:** line declares, all marked (create) and all new. Nothing named in ### Out of scope is touched: no plugin/scripts/ct-groom.mjs, groom.js, slices.js or gh-issue-map.js, no --reconcile or Project v2, no dispatcher or gate 1 change, no merge and no write to a pull request, no repository column on the milestone or on the dry run's product. Inside the files, every line serves a sentence of the task: no refactor of a neighbouring module, no helper without a user - each of the twelve mother scenarios and its ten exported constants is consumed by client.test.ts or useEpicGroom.test.ts. The staged diff carries no hunk of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-330-the-groom-and-gate-2.md, so there is no amendment to rule on and the plan's task 11 text and the brief agree.

Eight new tests, and the three properties that block hold for each. Deterministic: no real clock (vi.useFakeTimers plus advanceTimersByTimeAsync), no network (fetch is stubbed in every test), no filesystem, no randomness and no sleep standing in for synchronisation; every expected value is a literal fixture. Isolated: afterEach unstubs the globals and restores real timers, @testing-library/react's auto cleanup unmounts the hook because vite.config.ts sets globals: true, no file, port or directory is taken for granted and no test depends on another's order or state. Verifies real behaviour: each assertion is on what client.ts returned or on the request useEpicGroom.ts made or did not make through the doubled boundary - none is on a constant the test just defined. For the finer half I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and read its testing-anti-patterns.md reference. Two remarks, declared here and deliberately not reported as findings because both are the plan's own text rather than the implementer's choice: the skill's 'Minimal | One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' bites the TDD test's name, which the **TDD:** line dictates word for word, and the seven cases looped inside it('each of the seven states is read as its own kind'), which the **Tests:** line names as one test. Anti-Pattern 4 (incomplete mocks) is satisfied: the mother mirrors the complete documented body, not only the keys each test reads, and the describe names backend/API.md as the provenance of those shapes.
